hints: Picture the journey of one red blood cell starting at the heart, going to the lungs, back to the heart, then out to the body and back again. How many times does it visit the heart?
Be careful with the words. A cardiac cycle is just one heartbeat (about 0.8 s), while a complete circuit of the body is the whole long journey around both loops.
walkthrough:
**See the two separate loops**

Think of the mammalian heart as a double pump in the middle. One loop goes heart to lungs and back (pulmonary circulation). The other loop goes heart to body and back (systemic circulation).

**Do not mix up cycle and circuit**

A cardiac cycle is one heartbeat: atria contract, ventricles contract, then all relax. A complete circuit of the body is much longer. It is the full trip around both the lung loop and the body loop.

**Count the visits to the heart**

In one full circuit, blood passes through the heart twice. Once on its way to the lungs to pick up oxygen, and a second time on its way to the body to deliver oxygen. That is why we call it double circulation.

options.A: This mixes up terms. In one cardiac cycle (one heartbeat) blood does not flow twice through the heart, it is just pumped once out of each side.
options.B: This is the definition of double circulation. Blood passes through the heart twice for every one complete trip around the pulmonary plus systemic circuits.
options.C: This describes a closed circulation, where blood stays inside vessels. Mammals have this, but it does not explain why it is double.
options.D: Blood does carry both gases, but that is a transport function. It is true, yet it is not the reason for the term double circulation.
